clue.text: Anticlimax, lawyer getting Cameron to return dated satirical article

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer

explanation.surface: A satirical magazine pokes fun at a lawyer being handed over to David Cameron, and the whole affair fizzles out.
explanation.definitionFit: A damp squib is a firework that fails to go off, hence any event that disappoints expectations.

explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts MM inside E and A; 'twice' doubles the M.
explanation.definitionFit: A luvvie is a theatrical actor; a familiar way to name one is by first name only, as with Thompson.

clue.text: Covered in piss, must broadcast misinformation

clue.text: Sick Blair, according to Eye, back recruiting timid types — "topping"

clue.text: Brenda's place to back Miliband's shrunken lot — honest!

explanation.definitionFit: Balmoral Castle in Aberdeenshire is a private royal residence, so it is the Queen's place.

clue.text: Put power in piss and get it all over the place

clue.text: "Every year one must utter it: it gets one's member back working"

definitions.text: "Every year one must utter it: it gets one's member back working"

parts.words: Every year one must utter it: it gets one's member back working
parts.note: surface reading: a routine that restores a man's flagging member to working order; setter's reading: the monarch, the royal 'one', reads an annual address that sets members of Parliament back to work

explanation.walkthrough: The royal 'one' is the monarch's speech habit; member means a Member of Parliament, not a body part. The address opens each new parliamentary session.
explanation.definitionFit: The monarch's address at the State Opening sets out the government's programme as Parliament resumes business.

clue.text: Looking at a looker's organ, intercourse follows
